title: Externship vs. Internship: What's the Difference? (2027)
summary: Shadowing or real work, a few days or a whole summer, unpaid or paid: how the two compare, plus what 409 extern postings on Simplify show about who offers them.
body_markdown:
An externship is usually a short, observation-focused experience, from a single day to a few weeks, where you shadow professionals to see what a job is like. An internship is longer, usually a summer or a semester, and you do real work for the team, often for pay. In healthcare the line blurs: most externships posted on Simplify right now are paid, hands-on programs for nursing and veterinary students.


This post covers the general difference first, then what 409 externship postings on Simplify show about who actually offers them.


## Externship vs. internship at a glance


**Externship** **Internship**


**Length** A day to a few weeks (clinical externships can run a summer) Usually 8 to 12 weeks in summer, or a semester


**What you do** Mostly **shadowing and observing** **Real work** on the team's projects


**Pay** Often unpaid, except in healthcare Usually paid at large companies


**Academic credit** Sometimes, often arranged by your school Sometimes, if your program offers it


**Who sets it up** Often your school or alumni network Usually the employer, through an application


**Best for** **Exploring** a career before you commit **Building experience** for your resume and a full-time offer


**Common fields** Healthcare, veterinary medicine, law, education Every field


## What is an externship?


An externship gives you a close look at a job without the responsibility of doing it. You might follow a lawyer through a day of meetings, sit in on a hospital unit's rounds, or spend a week rotating through a company's teams. Many universities run externship programs during winter or spring break and match students with alumni.


The goal is to answer one question: do I want to do this work? Because externships are short, you can try several fields in a single year.


## What is an internship?


An internship is a temporary job, usually for students or recent graduates. You are given real tasks, a manager and often a project to finish by the end. Internships at large companies are usually paid, and a strong internship is one of the most common paths to a full-time offer.


## What we see on Simplify


We looked at every US job posting on Simplify with "extern" or "externship" in the title on November 24, 2026, and kept the 409 listed as internship-type roles.


- **Almost all are in healthcare.** 195 were veterinary externships (48%), 112 were nursing (27%) and 73 were other healthcare roles such as audiology, MRI and surgical technology (18%). Only 4 were legal externships, and 25 were in other fields, including CS and IT, culinary and finance.
- **Many are paid.** 41% listed pay. Of the 164 with an hourly rate, the median was about $18 an hour, and the middle half ranged from $15 to $26.
- **A few employers post most of them.** One veterinary group, Alliance Animal Health, had 120 open externships on its own, so the veterinary share partly reflects one large employer.


Two notes on scope. These are only externships posted as jobs, so school-run programs that match students with alumni do not appear here, and those are the ones most likely to be short and unpaid. And postings without a listed rate are not counted in the pay figures.


## In healthcare, an externship is often a paid job


If you are a nursing, veterinary or allied health student, "externship" usually means something closer to an internship. Hospitals and clinics hire students to work alongside licensed staff, often over the summer, for an hourly wage. A nurse externship, for example, is typically for nursing students partway through their program, who support patient care under an RN's supervision.


If you are outside healthcare, assume an externship is short and unpaid unless the posting says otherwise.


## Externship vs. internship: which should you choose?


If you... Choose


Are not sure which career you want An **externship** , or several in different fields


Know the field and need experience for your resume An **internship**


Need to earn money over the summer A **paid internship** , or a paid clinical externship if you are in healthcare


Are a nursing, veterinary or allied health student A **clinical externship** , which works like an internship


Have a winter or spring break free A school-run **externship**


You do not have to pick one. A common path is an externship freshman or sophomore year to explore, then an internship the summer after to build experience.


## How to find externships and internships


- **Your school's career center.** Most externship programs run through schools, especially alumni shadowing programs.
- **Hospitals and clinics.** Search the careers page of health systems near you for "extern" or "student nurse."
- **Simplify.** Search Simplify's[job board](https://simplify.jobs/jobs?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=externship-vs-internship&utm_content=body-1) for "externship" or browse curated lists like[Freshman and Sophomore Internships](https://simplify.jobs/l/Freshman-and-Sophomore-Internships?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=externship-vs-internship&utm_content=body-2) . The free[Job Tracker](https://simplify.jobs/job-application-tracker?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=externship-vs-internship&utm_content=find) keeps track of where you applied, and the free[Copilot](https://simplify.jobs/copilot?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=cta&utm_campaign=externship-vs-internship&utm_content=find) extension fills out applications for you.


Simplify is used by more than 2 million job seekers. In a 2022 survey of Harvard CS students it ranked among the top three places they found tech internships ([Harvard career center, archived](https://web.archive.org/web/20240228134502/https://careerservices.fas.harvard.edu/blog/2022/11/22/beyond-big-tech-where-can-i-find-summer-opportunities/) ), and the University of Washington's career center[recommends it](https://careers.uw.edu/resources/simplify/?ref=blog.simplify.jobs) for applying faster.


## Common questions


**What is the difference between an externship and an internship?** An externship is usually short, from a day to a few weeks, and focused on shadowing. An internship is usually a summer or semester of real work, and is more often paid. In healthcare, externships are often paid and hands-on too.


**What is an extern?** An extern is a person doing an externship. In hospitals, a nurse extern is a nursing student working with patients under the supervision of a registered nurse.


**Are externships paid?** Outside healthcare, usually not. In healthcare, often yes: of the externship postings on Simplify on November 24, 2026 that listed pay, the median was about $18 an hour.


**Does an externship count as experience on a resume?** Yes. List it under experience with the dates and what you observed or did. Be accurate: write "shadowed" or "observed" for a shadowing externship, not "managed" or "led."


**Can you do an externship and an internship in the same year?** Yes. Externships often fit into winter or spring break, so they can come before a summer internship.
